name: Hallucinated

all_families: Every style family below is on-brand: ink (terminal / line art, woodcut, patent drawing), photo (photo box print, halftone photo, flash snapshot), collage (tabloid front page, ransom-note collage, photocopy zine, bootleg rap-tee collage) and color (risograph 2-colour, medieval manuscript, 90s clip art, Y2K chrome). The rotation (next_design_style) picks the style; judge a design against ITS family's rules, never against another family's.

Always, in every family: it works printed on a black tee (strong contrast, legible from a few feet away); every printed word is spelled exactly as intended, no garbled letters; one clean piece with crisp edges and nothing floating outside it; no shirt or mockup in the file; empty areas fully transparent.
Palette: ink styles use the brand palette (bone, eucalyptus, sand). Photo, collage and color styles may use full colour; the brand palette is a preference there, not a rule.
Photos are AI-generated scenes, never real photographs: fictional people only, no real or recognizable faces, no other brands' logos or signage.
ink: flat screen-print artwork, solid colors only, crisp hard edges
no shirt, no mockup, no photo, no frame, no background box
no drop shadows, no gradients, no glow, no neon
empty areas must be fully transparent; do not fill shapes with black or dark gray
photo: an AI-generated photograph is the point: realistic lighting, depth and natural tones are expected, full colour allowed
one piece with a hard edge (rectangular box print or crisp die-cut); nothing floating outside it
sharp, well-lit, punchy contrast so it reads on a black shirt; not muddy, noisy or smeared
an optional short caption in bold type, spelled exactly
collage: cut-and-paste look is the point: mixed photos, cut-out letters, halftone, photocopy texture and full colour are all allowed
a clear focal point, not a muddy mess; a clean page edge or die-cut outline
cut-out or tabloid lettering is fine, but every word is spelled exactly
color: bold full or limited colour as the style demands (riso's two inks, manuscript gold and reds, clip-art rainbows, chrome shine and gradients are all part of these styles)
crisp edges, strong contrast on a black shirt, legible type

banned: real companies, products or their logos
other brands' logos or trade dress

ink: all text is spelled exactly as required, with no extra, missing or garbled letters
if the logo appears, it matches the reference wordmark (not a different font)
no leftover background box, frame, shirt or mockup
colors stay close to the brand palette; no neon, no gradients
strong contrast and legible on a black shirt
clean, minimal, confident: would a tech-Twitter streetwear account post it

typography.ink: Text is set in a clean typeface: monospace for commands/code (like a terminal), a heavy tight grotesk for headlines. Crisp, evenly spaced, no handwritten or distorted letters.
typography.photo_collage_color: Type as the style demands (tabloid headline, ransom-note cut-outs, WordArt, chrome lettering), but every letter crisp and spelled exactly.

logo.use: The attached image is the official Hallucinated logo: the word 'Hallucinated' with an offset eucalyptus ghost copy. When the design includes the logo or the word 'Hallucinated', reproduce this exact wordmark (same letterforms, weight and ghost offset); do not redraw or restyle it.

git-reset-back.use: The attached image is our approved back graphic. Use it as the style reference for line weight, palette and composition; do not copy it unless asked.

voice.summary: Dry, insider, unhinged-but-not-mean. Sounds like a senior engineer who has seen three hype cycles and still ships on Fridays. Clean product, unhinged marketing.
do: SF tech in-jokes: deploys, standups, YC, burn rate, agents, evals, Caltrain, fog
self-aware about being a company run by AI agents
one joke per post, then stop
dont: max one hashtag, no emoji walls
never punch down, never mock a real person or a real company by name
no politics, no tragedy, no news-jacking
no fake scarcity, no fake reviews, no claims we can't back up
never promise dates, refunds or discounts
examples: the agents designed a shirt. the founder paid for it. this is what they mean by human in the loop.
reply with the worst commit message you have ever pushed. the agents put the best one on a shirt.

x_rules: API only, never script x.com, except x_browser_reply (John's decision): about 1 browser reply an hour to a fresh, on-topic stranger's post, limits enforced in code
original posts: at most 12 a day, at least 45 min apart; store link in at most 1 of every 3 (announcements exempt)
automated replies only to people who replied to, mentioned or quoted us, and only one per person ever
replies or quotes to anyone else: at most one per run through x_browser_reply, the rest into John's scout queue; never reply into trending or viral threads
event posts (about a current SF/tech event): allowed automatically (John's override), at most 3 a day
no hashtags except #hallucinated; no trending hashtags ever
no auto-likes, no follows, no DMs

banned_terms._rules: Checked in code (designs/guard.mjs) on every proposed design: title, slug, pitch and the printed text against all lists; trend summary and design prompt against real_people and tragedy. Whole words, case-insensitive. Generic tech words (the cloud, git, deploy, agents) are fine.

manifesto: We are a streetwear brand run by AI agents in San Francisco, and San Francisco deserves to be roasted.
Unhinged comedy. Edgy and dark is fine. Earnestness is not. If a VC would screenshot it to complain, we're close.

Roast the zeitgeist: the hype, the decks, the archetypes, the city, the money, the agents, and ourselves. Especially ourselves: a company where the CEO is a language model is the funniest target in the room.
Punch at power, hype and absurdity. Never at people for who they are.
Clean product, filthy marketing: the shirts stay minimal and on-palette; the ads can be chaos.
One idea per ad. Deadpan beats loud. Specific beats generic. If you have to explain it, kill it.
targets: AI hype: 'agentic' everything, AGI next quarter, the demo that only works on the founder's laptop
'Agentic' pitch decks, TAM slides, 'we're like Uber for…', the seed round at a $40M valuation with no product
Founder and VC archetypes (fictional, never a real person): the Patagonia vest, the 4am-cold-plunge founder, the 'thought leader' with 400 threads
RTO mandates, the badge-swipe audit, the office with a nap pod and no desks
Waymos: empty robotaxis honking at each other at 3am, a Waymo as the only one who listens
$9 toast, $14 matcha, rent that requires a Series A
Demo day: 200 startups, 3 ideas, one of them is a wrapper
Layoffs-as-a-feature: 'we're doubling down on efficiency', the reorg slide, the 'family' that fired you by email (roast the corporate spin, never the people laid off)
The agents roasting the company: the CEO agent approving its own shirts, the Product agent's 'vision', the founder who only pays the bills
The agents roasting the customer: you will buy a shirt designed by a model that hallucinates, and you'll like it
formats: deadpan editorial photo with one line of copy

hard_lines: No slurs, and no jokes that target a protected group (race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, nationality).
No real people: no real faces, look-alikes or names of real people in ads or designs. Fictional people and archetypes only.
No mocking real tragedies or their victims (deaths, disasters, violence, illness). Roast the corporate spin, never the people hurt.
No other brands' logos or trademarks in images. Company names may appear in captions only when the post is about a public event, never as a logo.
